name: Aruba
summary: The Landsbesluit lijkenvervoer (AB 1993 GT 36, implementing art. 40 of the Begrafenisverordening) allows a body to be brought into Aruba if it is embalmed or otherwise preserved, sealed in a hermetic impermeable coffin with absorbent material inside a sound outer case, labelled, and accompanied by a medical/death statement, an embalming statement and a transport statement from the authority of the place of death. Burial must take place as soon as possible with written leave from the civil registrar.
documents: Medical statement from the competent doctor where the death occurred, or an extract of the death certificate (name, birth date/age, date and place of death, cause of death or statement that death was natural / not due to a contagious disease)
Statement from the person who embalmed or otherwise preserved the body, describing the method used
Statement from the competent authority of the place of death on how and by which route the body will be transported (transfer permit)
Strasbourg 1973 laissez-passer when coming from a Strasbourg Agreement state (explicitly recognised in the cremation rules)
Passport or ID copy of the deceased (practice; confirm with the funeral home)
coffin: Hermetically sealed coffin made of impermeable material (zinc-lined in practice) with absorbent material, containing only the body, its clothing, packing material and personal effects, packed to the satisfaction of the doctor designated by the Minister of Public Works and Public Health in a well-closing outer coffin. Name, first names, date of birth, date and place of death and destination must be clearly marked on the coffin. The law does not say who must witness the sealing at origin.
embalming: Required: the body must be embalmed or properly preserved by another method. If the death was due to a quarantinable disease, arterial and cavity embalming is mandatory.
consular: No specific consular step is set by the law; the transport statement must come from the competent authority of the country of death. As part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (a Hague Apostille party), apostilled foreign documents are the norm; confirm translation needs with the receiving funeral home.
arrival: Documents are presented on arrival; customs and the health authority clear the coffin. Bodies brought into Aruba must be buried as soon as possible and only with free written leave from the civil registrar (ambtenaar van de burgerlijke stand), which cannot be issued before the death statement is produced. For cremation, the customs officer must receive the Strasbourg laissez-passer (if from a party state) or an equivalent statement from the origin authority, and cremation takes place as soon as possible after 5 working days.
private_aviation: No published rule specific to private aircraft. A private flight must land at the international airport with customs and health clearance; the same coffin and document rules apply as for cargo. Arrange collection by a local funeral home at the airport.
private_jet_note: Coffin must be hermetically sealed and labelled; have the three statements in hand for customs on landing.
export: Leaving Aruba: the same rules apply in reverse. The body must be embalmed or preserved, sealed in a hermetic impermeable coffin with absorbent material inside an outer case to the satisfaction of the doctor designated by the Minister of Public Works and Public Health, labelled, and accompanied by the medical/death statement, the embalming statement and a transport statement for the authorities of the destination. Exhumed remains travel in a hermetically sealed coffin with the exhumation permit where required. Typical delay is not published; local funeral homes usually need a few working days.
export_points: Embalming or other preservation is mandatory
Hermetic impermeable coffin inside an outer case, approved by the designated doctor
Death/medical statement, embalming statement and transport statement must travel with the body
Delay not published; allow several working days

at_a_glance.death_certificate: Death statement or certificate extract required
at_a_glance.consular: No consular step set by law
at_a_glance.permit: Civil registrar burial leave on arrival

steps.what: Funeral home at origin obtains death certificate/medical statement and embalms the body.
Origin authority issues transport permit stating route; documents apostilled if needed.
Body sealed in hermetic coffin inside outer case, labelled with identity and destination.
Documents presented to customs/health at the airport; local funeral home collects.
Civil registrar issues written burial leave; burial as soon as possible.

key_points: Hermetic sealing and preservation are legal requirements, so a pouch alone is not acceptable
Aruba is a country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands with its own legislation; Dutch European rules do not apply directly.
Burial must take place as soon as possible after arrival
Aruba's cremation decree recognises the Strasbourg 1973 laissez-passer
authority: Directie Volksgezondheid (Ministry of Public Health) and the Civil Registry (Burgerlijke Stand), Aruba

name: Belize
summary: Belize does not publish official entry requirements for a casket online; confirm with the Belize consulate or embassy and a licensed funeral home. Expect a death certificate, embalming certificate and transit permit (English-language documents accepted).
documents: Death certificate from the country of death (apostilled; English is an official language of Belize)
Embalming certificate
Transit / burial-transit permit from the country of death
Passport or ID of the deceased
coffin: No official published entry rule found; assume a sealed, airline-compliant casket.
embalming: Not officially published for entry; embalming is standard for international shipment.
consular: Belize consulates and embassies are the point of contact. Belize is a Hague Apostille party; no translation needed for English documents.
arrival: Customs and health clearance at Philip S. W. Goldson International Airport; a local funeral home collects. Burial deadline not officially published.
private_aviation: No official rule for private or charter flights carrying human remains was found. Plan arrival at an international airport with customs and health officers, and confirm clearance with the local funeral home and airport authority before departure.
private_jet_note: Entry rules unpublished: confirm health and customs clearance with the consulate before take-off.
export: Leaving Belize: local undertakers register the death with the Vital Statistics Unit and arrange a Belize death certificate to accompany the remains. A post-mortem is normally performed in all cases and always when death is not natural; a Coroner (usually a magistrate) investigates unnatural deaths. Personal belongings cannot be shipped with the body. Mortuaries are at regional hospitals; standards vary.

Post-mortem normally performed in all cases
Coroner involved for unnatural deaths
Personal belongings cannot travel with the body

documents: Death certificate from the country of death, apostilled or legalised, with Spanish translation (confirm with consulate)
Embalming certificate
Transit / burial-transit permit from the country of death
Passport or ID of the deceased
coffin: No official published entry rule found. The British Embassy notes that local funeral directors supply the special caskets required for international carriage of human remains; a sealed, airline-compliant casket should be assumed.
embalming: Embalming is commonly used for international shipment (British Embassy). Entry requirement not officially published.
consular: Guatemalan consulates abroad coordinate repatriations of Guatemalan nationals; Guatemala is a Hague Apostille party, so the foreign death certificate should be apostilled and translated into Spanish. Confirm with the consulate.
arrival: Customs and health clearance at the airport of entry; a local funeral home collects. Local custom is burial within 24 hours (British Embassy), so arrange the receiving funeral home in advance.

In violent or suspicious deaths the Ministerio Publico (prosecutor) investigates and an autopsy is required, which can delay release; otherwise the body is usually released within a few days. Cold storage is scarce outside Guatemala City.
